name: application-heatmap-calendar
title: Heatmap Calendar
description: A GitHub-style contribution grid that maps activity intensity onto a calendar of small colored cells, with month labels and a Less–More legend.
useWhen: Summarizing daily activity intensity across many weeks or months in one glanceable grid.
The exact date and value per cell matter less than the overall pattern of frequency or streaks over time.
avoidWhen: Users need to pick or view a specific date — use the `calendar` component instead.
The data has few enough points that a bar or line chart from `charts` would be more precise and just as compact.
responsiveBehavior: The grid scrolls horizontally inside its own overflow container on narrow viewports rather than shrinking cells below a legible size; wrap it in `overflow-x-auto` in constrained layouts.
accessibility: Cell intensity is conveyed by both color and a five-step Less–More legend so the scale isn't color-only.
Pair each cell with a title attribute or tooltip stating the exact date and count in a real implementation — the static color alone is not sufficient for screen reader users.
Weekday and month labels stay visible so the grid can be read positionally, not just by hue.

variants.title: Contribution grid
variants.description: A five-month, five-level intensity grid with weekday and month labels and a Less–More legend.
accessibility: In production, give each cell an accessible name with the date and count rather than relying on color alone.

variants.title: Contribution grid (Dark)
variants.description: Contribution grid adapted for dark surfaces, with intensity ramping toward a brighter emerald at the high end.
accessibility: Cell intensity steps remain visually distinguishable at dark-mode contrast levels.
